name: CUET-UG

cycle_2026.fee: Up to 3 subjects: ₹1,000 (Gen), ₹900 (OBC-NCL/EWS), ₹800 (SC/ST/PwBD/Third gender), ₹4,500 (outside India); each extra subject ₹400 / ₹375 / ₹350 / ₹1,800

cycle_2027: Not announced yet (2026 notice came out 3 Jan 2026, so expect early Jan 2027)
eligibility: Class XII passed or appearing in 2026; no age limit for CUET. Each university sets its own programme eligibility (e.g. DU requires CUET subjects you studied in Class XII; BMS/BBA FIA need Maths in XII).

sections.name: Languages (13 options, e.g. English, Hindi)
sections.notes: Reading comprehension (factual, literary, narrative passages), literary aptitude, vocabulary

sections.name: Domain subjects (23 options, e.g. Mathematics/Applied Maths, Accountancy, Business Studies, Economics)
sections.notes: Based on NCERT Class XII syllabus

sections.name: General Aptitude Test
sections.notes: GK, current affairs, mental ability, numerical ability, quant reasoning (arithmetic, algebra, geometry, mensuration, statistics), logical and analytical reasoning

pattern.notes: Since 2025: 37 subjects in total (13 languages + 23 domain + 1 General Aptitude Test); old Section IA/IB/II/III labels dropped and no optional questions. Pick up to 5 subjects. Each paper is a separate 60-min test with 50 compulsory questions. Multi-shift papers are normalised into NTA scores.

selection_process: No single CUET merit list. Each university decides which CUET subject combination counts for each programme and runs its own counselling (DU: CSAS; BHU, AU, UoH etc.: own portals). DU (2026): BMS / BBA (FIA) = one language + Maths/Applied Maths + one List B subject + General Aptitude Test (SSCBS FAQ). B.Com (Hons) = one language + Maths/Applied Maths or Accountancy + two subjects, best combination counts. BA (Hons) Economics = one language + Maths/Applied Maths + two subjects. B.Com (pass) = language + 3 subjects OR language + 1 subject + General Aptitude Test. Class XII marks are used only for tie-breaks at DU. St. Stephen's minority seats add an interview (85% CUET + 15% interview).
verbal_weight: Language paper (usually English) = 1 of the 3–4 papers most universities count (e.g. 250 of ~1,000 marks for DU BMS); General Aptitude Test has no separate English section

notes: 185 universities used CUET-UG 2026 (48 central, 33 state, 23 deemed, 76 private, 5 other). DU CSAS 2026: 71,624 UG seats, 2.18 L registrations; Round 1 on 16–17 Jul, Round 2 on 25 Jul, Round 3 on 8 Aug, then spot rounds. DU scores here are 'minimum allocation scores' (the last score admitted in that round). They usually fall in later rounds. Compare only within the same year and programme, because the number of papers counted differs between programmes. NOT via CUET: Jamia Millia Islamia (B.Com Hons, BBA, BA Hons Eco use JMI's own entrance test), AMU (B.Com Hons via AMU admission test), JNU (no BBA/BCom/Eco UG; CUET only for BA foreign languages). Private and deemed universities on NTA's 2026 CUET list that offer in-scope programmes include Bennett, Azim Premji, BML Munjal, Mahindra, Alliance, Chanakya, Rishihood, UPES, Manipal Jaipur, Amity, Sharda, Galgotias, Jamia Hamdard, TERI SAS, ICFAI Hyderabad, and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar School of Economics University Bengaluru. Shiv Nadar, Christ and Symbiosis are not on NTA's list (they run their own tests). Check each university's own CUET subject rule before choosing your 5 subjects.
